assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editors turn a DNA-modifying enzyme chemistry (cytidine and engineered adenosine deamination) into a programmable way to rewrite single bases without double-strand breaks. This converts a biological process into a defined chemical reaction and gives biologists a general tool, with direct genome-maintenance and disease relevance. Originality is high, especially the engineered deoxyadenosine deaminase, which has no natural counterpart.
assessment.attribution: Liu is the intellectual driver of both the cytosine and adenine base editors; Komor and Gaudelli were the lead experimentalists on the two editors. Credit within the Liu laboratory is clear. The Kondo/Nishida Target-AID work is parallel and independent, so a three-person prize would leave out a real contribution. Whether Liu should be recognized alone or with the first authors is a committee judgment.
assessment.maturity: Clinical-stage and first-in-human results exist and many independent laboratories use the tools. The core concept has been stable for roughly a decade. Timing is reasonable, though a CRISPR-adjacent recognition has to be weighed against the 2020 prize.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2020 CRISPR prize may weigh against it.
Long-term in vivo safety, bystander edits and off-target deamination are not fully settled.
Credit for Target-AID (Kondo, Nishida) is separate from the Liu laboratory work.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation gives a chemical mechanism, induced proximity to an E3 ligase, that reprograms cellular protein turnover. PROTACs and molecular glues give biologists and medicinal chemists a new class of reagents and drugs. The concept is original and the mechanism is well defined at the level of ternary-complex structures and kinetics.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies founded the PROTAC concept. Ciulli made the structure-guided design and VHL ligand work that made it practical. Handa and Ito identified cereblon as the thalidomide target, which explains molecular glue degraders, so the glue branch has a separate lineage that a three-name prize cannot cover. Sakamoto, Kim and Gray are further contributors. The allocation is unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Many clinical trials are in progress, and the mechanism has been confirmed independently in many laboratories. Approved degrader drugs are not yet in routine use, so the translational payoff is not complete.
uncertainties: PROTAC and molecular glue lineages (Crews/Deshaies versus Handa/Ito) may need different recognition.
No approved PROTAC drug yet, to my knowledge.
Eight credited names make a fair three-person configuration difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Mass-spectrometry proteomics made quantitative, system-wide measurement of proteins routine. As someone who relies on LC-MS/MS quantification of metabolite pools, I regard it as foundational measurement chemistry. The discoveries are broadly enabling, though most are methodological. The Nobel award for electrospray and MALDI in 2002 was the ionization step; the quantitative and large-scale layer is distinct.
assessment.attribution: Mann (high-resolution quantitative proteomics, SILAC), Aebersold (targeted and quantitative proteomics, SRM and SWATH) and Yates (shotgun and database-search proteomics) are the most widely cited leaders. Hunt, Gygi and Heck each made decisive contributions, so excluding them is contentious.
assessment.maturity: Methods are used extensively and independently confirmed, with strong clinical and biological uptake. The field is mature and recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Several comparable contributors (Hunt, Gygi, Heck) would be omitted.
Whether the committee views this as chemistry rather than biology/technology.
Partial overlap with the 2002 mass spectrometry prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Reading nucleic-acid sequences by single-molecule current blockades through a nanopore is a new analytical measurement principle, a physical readout of chemistry at the single-molecule level. Nanopore sequencing is now widely deployed and has opened long-read, direct RNA and modified-base detection, which is relevant for nucleic-acid biochemistry.
assessment.attribution: The founding idea and the early experiments came from Deamer, Branton and Akeson (1989-96) and from Kasianowicz and Bayley's alpha-hemolysin demonstration. Akeson showed enzyme-controlled, base-resolved ratcheting. Bayley's engineered pores and chemistry also matter. I believe Branton and Bayley have died, and that would limit eligibility; I have not verified this. The proposed set uses living people as I understand it.
assessment.maturity: The technology is commercial, independently verified and widely adopted, and the principle has been confirmed repeatedly. Accuracy limits remain, but the principle is stable.
uncertainties: Eligibility, because I am not certain which credited people are alive.
Distribution of credit among the founders (Branton, Deamer, Akeson) and Bayley/Kasianowicz is disputed.
Chemistry versus physics or biotechnology classification.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Orthogonal aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase/tRNA pairs allow site-specific incorporation of non-natural amino acids in living cells, which extends the genetic code and lets chemistry be written into proteins. This is a general tool, conceptually original, and now routine. The use of engineered translation also gives a clear chemical mechanism.
assessment.attribution: Schultz established the central methodology with Wang, and Chin extended it to multiple codons, quadruplet decoding, orthogonal ribosomes and whole-genome recoding in E. coli. Yokoyama and Mehl contributed important work. A prize to Schultz, Chin and Wang is plausible but leaves out other work.
assessment.maturity: Replicated independently in numerous organisms and widely used, with applications in therapeutics. Recognition is timely, since the field is mature.
uncertainties: Whether Wang or Yokoyama or Mehl should be included.
The field's most impactful work, whole-genome recoding, is still developing.
Strength of translational payoff is still partial.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Pd-catalyzed C-N cross-coupling is a general, mechanistically well-understood reaction that is used in pharmaceutical synthesis and medicinal chemistry every day. Important as a tool for making the building blocks and drugs that biologists use. Its originality is moderate, because it builds on the earlier cross-coupling Nobel work (2010).
assessment.attribution: Buchwald and Hartwig independently developed the ligand-controlled, broadly applicable amination; Kosugi's tin amide chemistry was an early precursor. Two laureates seem to be a fair and clearly defined allocation, with Kosugi's precedent a minor open point.
assessment.maturity: Very mature, independently validated and widely adopted for decades. Recognition could be seen as overdue, though the 2010 Nobel prize for Pd cross-coupling may be viewed as having covered the area.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2010 palladium cross-coupling prize.
Role of Kosugi and Migita in priority.
Possible concern that this is an extension of an already recognized reaction class.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Activity-based protein profiling uses reactive probes to read the functional state of enzymes in complex proteomes. It ties chemical reactivity to biological function and has found new enzyme activities and druggable sites. The concept has strong chemical content and medical relevance for enzymology.
assessment.attribution: Cravatt is the central founder of the approach (serine hydrolase profiling) and its extension to cysteine reactivity profiling, while Bogyo and Overkleeft made decisive contributions for protease probes. Weerapana's credit derives largely from cysteine-reactivity work in the Cravatt group. Cravatt could be recognized alone or together with the others.
assessment.maturity: Independently adopted in industry and academia, and the concept is stable. Clinical impact through covalent ligand discovery is emerging but not complete.
uncertainties: Whether Bogyo and Overkleeft are equal contributors.
Impact is broad but diffuse across many applications.
Covalent drug discovery application is still emerging.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Massively parallel sequencing-by-synthesis uses reversible-terminator chemistry on clustered DNA and changed genetics and genome maintenance research. It is a chemical solution (nucleotide analogue design and surface chemistry) to a biological readout problem, with huge and measurable impact.
assessment.attribution: Balasubramanian and Klenerman developed the Solexa approach with the key chemistry (reversible terminators, single-molecule colonies). Rothberg (pyrosequencing, 454), Mayer and Ju contributed parallel or complementary technologies. Credit is complex because of commercial development and parallel platforms.
assessment.maturity: Technology is thoroughly validated and ubiquitous, so the maturity is very high. The long delay might reduce the novelty impression; the Nobel to Sanger already covered sequencing chemistry.
uncertainties: Credit among multiple parallel platforms (Solexa, 454, Mayer, Ju) is disputed.
Previous sequencing Nobel prizes (Sanger, 1980) may make the committee hesitant.
Chemistry versus biotechnology or medicine classification.
